items.capacity: Vice-Chair, Frontier AI Taskforce External Advisory Board
items.fact: GOV.UK press release of 7 September 2023 names Matt Clifford, Prime Minister's Representative for the AI Safety Summit, as External Advisory Board Vice-Chair of the Frontier AI Taskforce. The release gives the announcement date and no end date for the role.
items.publisher: GOV.UK (DSIT, AI Safety Institute, Michelle Donelan)
items.quote: Matt Clifford who will join as Vice-Chair
items.missing: End date of the vice-chair role, and whether it continued into 2026.
items.notes: Same release names Frontier AI Taskforce Chair Ian Hogarth ('Frontier AI Taskforce Chair, Ian Hogarth, said') and 'Alignment Research Centre Chief Paul Christiano' as board members (page read). The release is titled as a Taskforce announcement; the body was renamed AI Safety Institute and later AI Security Institute (Feb 2025, per AISI page note).

items.capacity: Member, AI Safety Institute Advisory Board
items.fact: Clifford's GOV.UK declared-interests record lists membership of the AI Safety Institute Advisory Board from 3 November 2023, with end marked Ongoing. The page read says 'Last updated: 12 February 2025', so it does not show the position in September 2026.
items.quote: Member of the AI Safety Institute Advisory Board 3 November 2023 Ongoing
items.missing: Whether the AISI advisory board membership was still held in September 2026, and whether it ended when he joined Anthropic: not found. No later version of the record was available to read.
items.notes: Same page (Feb 2025 version) contains a DSIT letter sentence: 'your role as the Vice-Chair of the Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute'. The same record lists Prime Minister's AI Opportunities Adviser, 13 January 2025 to 12 January 2026. Search snippets (not read) report he stepped down as ARIA chair on 7 September 2026, staying until 6 November 2026; none of the sources read says the AISI board seat ended.

items.capacity: Managing Director, International Affairs (government engagement outside North America)
items.fact: The Guardian (published 2 September 2026; syndicated copy read) reports Clifford has joined Anthropic as managing director of international affairs. The same article says Anthropic will have him recuse himself from any decisions affecting the company at ARIA.
items.quote: has joined US startup Anthropic as managing director of international affairs
items.missing: Anthropic's own announcement and exact start date. Whether the AISI advisory board seat (T8.2) continued after this move: not found.
items.notes: Guardian excerpt also says ARIA's chair role was under scrutiny from the Commons science committee chair (Chi Onwurah). Search snippets (not read): stepped down as ARIA chair 7 Sept 2026. Guardian says he 'previously served as Keir Starmer's AI opportunities adviser before stepping down'.

items.capacity: Chair, Foundation Model / Frontier AI Taskforce, then AI Safety Institute, then AI Security Institute
items.fact: DSIT declared-interests record (last updated 21 February 2025, page updated 24 February 2025) lists Hogarth as Chair of the AI Safety Institute (formerly the AI Foundation Model Taskforce) from 12 June 2023. It lists him as Chair of the AI Security Institute from 10 February 2025 to 9 December 2025.
items.quote: Chair of the AI Security Institute (formerly the AI Safety Institute)
items.missing: Any role after 9 December 2025, and whether that end date was a scheduled term or an actual departure. Any AI-company role: not found.
items.notes: The 9 December 2025 end date sits in a record last updated February 2025, so it is a scheduled term. A search snippet (not read in full) quotes the same record: 'During his appointment as chair, Ian Hogarth will continue his normal business activities including his duties to Plural.' A wiki source gives a February 2025 end date that conflicts; the gov.uk record is used here.

items.capacity: Founding Director, AI Security Institute; later Director General for Artificial Intelligence, Cabinet Office, head of the Prime Minister's AI Taskforce
items.fact: GOV.UK people page says Ollie Ilott is a founding Director of the AI Security Institute and was previously Director General for Emerging Technology and AI at DSIT. It says he was appointed Director General for Artificial Intelligence, Cabinet Office, in July 2026; no AI-company role is listed.
items.quote: Ollie is a founding Director of the AI Security Institute
items.missing: Start and end dates of the founding-director role (not given on the page). Search snippets (not read) conflict on his post dates.
items.notes: Search snippets (not read): an Interim Director General post from August 2025, and a single-outlet report that he was elected chair of the International Network of AI Safety Institutes (unverified). Page date not shown in the read.

items.from: U.S. Department of Commerce (Secretary Gina Raimondo)
items.capacity: Head of AI Safety, U.S. AI Safety Institute (NIST)
items.fact: CDO Magazine (updated 19 April 2024) reports that Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo announced Paul Christiano as head of AI safety for the U.S. AI Safety Institute, overseeing tests of cutting-edge models. The NIST profile and release links I tried returned 404, so no NIST primary source was read.
items.quote: Paul Christiano as U.S. AI Safety Institute's (AISI) Head of AI Safety
items.missing: End date of this post; a NIST primary source (not reachable). Search snippet (not read) says he returned to ARC in August 2026, single source, unverified.
items.notes: Christiano was also named on the 2023-09-07 UK Taskforce External Advisory Panel ('Alignment Research Centre Chief Paul Christiano'); see T8.7 for his Anthropic trusteeship.

items.capacity: Initial Trustee, Anthropic Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.fact: Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust page (published 19 September 2023) lists Paul Christiano among the initial Trustees. A footnote on the same page lists previous Trustees with step-down dates, including Paul Christiano (April 2024).
items.quote: Paul Christiano : Founder of the Alignment Research Center
items.missing: Independent confirmation of the April 2024 step-down date (the page is Anthropic's own statement); reason for leaving not stated.
items.notes: Anthropic's page describes the LTBT as 'an independent body comprising five Trustees'. The page is updated to October 2026 and lists current Trustees; Christiano is not among them. Search snippet (not read) says Christiano left the trust before taking the AISI post; the exact timing is not independently verified.

items.from: UK AI Safety Institute and U.S. AI Safety Institute
items.capacity: Joint pre-deployment evaluation of upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet (released 22 October 2024)
items.fact: UK AISI page (dated 19 November 2024; read) says the UK and US AI Safety Institutes 'conducted a joint pre-deployment evaluation' of Anthropic's upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet, released 22 October 2024. The page notes the UK body was renamed AI Security Institute on 14 February 2025.
items.publisher: UK AI Security Institute (formerly AI Safety Institute)
items.quote: conducted a joint pre-deployment evaluation of Anthropic's latest model
items.missing: The US-side report (a nist.gov document, seen in search results, not opened); exact evaluation dates within the page.
items.notes: Search results (not read) list a NIST document titled as a joint testing report on upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet, dated 19 November 2024 in its file name. Search summary (not read) says the review covered biological and cyber capabilities; not verified on the page.

items.from: U.S. AI Safety Institute (NIST, Department of Commerce)
items.capacity: Memorandum of Understanding on AI safety research, testing and evaluation; access to major new models before and after public release
items.fact: NIST release (dated 29 August 2024; read) says Anthropic's Memorandum of Understanding 'establishes the framework' for the U.S. AI Safety Institute to receive access to major new models before and after public release. The same page says the institute was re-established as CAISI in June 2025.
items.quote: establishes the framework for the U.S. AI Safety Institute to receive access
items.missing: MoU text; term, renewal and status after the June 2025 re-establishment as CAISI; whether access continued into 2026.
items.notes: NIST quotes Elizabeth Kelly, then director: 'we look forward to beginning our technical collaborations with Anthropic and OpenAI'. A secondary search snippet (not read) says the MoUs were reaffirmed under CAISI; unverified. Kelly's move to Anthropic is item T8.12.

items.capacity: Pre-release test access for Claude Mythos 5.1 declined (reported)
items.fact: eWeek (10 September 2026; read) reports Anthropic declined to let the UK AI Security Institute test Claude Mythos 5.1 before release, citing people familiar with the matter who spoke to the Financial Times. A Cabinet Office statement quoted there says AISI 'continues to collaborate closely with industry partners, including Anthropic'.
items.quote: Anthropic declined to let Britain's AI safety watchdog test Claude Mythos 5.1 before release.
items.missing: The FT original; whether UK researchers later received Mythos 5.1; Anthropic's stated reason. Single secondary outlet.
items.notes: eWeek also says AISI 'had previously worked with Anthropic on advanced model evaluations', and that in September 2025 Anthropic said government researchers received systems at multiple stages of development. Neither side has said the relationship is over (per eWeek).

items.capacity: Partner in the GBP 15m Alignment Project (international AI alignment research initiative)
items.fact: UKTN (30 July 2025; read) reports the UK AI Security Institute launched a joint initiative with Amazon, Anthropic and the Canadian government's equivalent body, backed by GBP 15m. Anthropic's Jack Clark is quoted; the page gives no Anthropic money or compute figure.
items.quote: Anthropic is delighted to work with the UK AI Security Institute
items.missing: Official gov.uk or AISI launch release; Anthropic's compute terms and value (a search headline, not read, says Anthropic joined to contribute compute resources).
items.notes: Money-flow check: no AISI grant, contract or payment to or from Anthropic was found in the searches. Other backers on the page: Halcyon Futures, Safe AI Fund, UKRI, Schmidt Sciences, ARIA. A separate DSIT-Anthropic public-services deal (Feb 2025, search headline, not read) is government, not AISI.

items.fact: Concordia staff listing (read; undated) says Elizabeth Kelly 'is Head of Beneficial Deployments at Anthropic' and was founding Director of the U.S. AI Safety Institute. Insurance Journal (Reuters, 6 February 2025; read) reports she was departing her role as the institute's inaugural director.
items.quote: Elizabeth Kelly is Head of Beneficial Deployments at Anthropic
items.missing: Anthropic's own confirmation; start date of the Anthropic role. The Anthropic link rests on one third-party listing.
items.notes: Insurance Journal (6 Feb 2025) quotes 'The U.S. AI Safety Institute's inaugural director, Elizabeth Kelly, is departing her role on Wednesday'. Other movers, not_found: no further AISI or Taskforce staff joining Anthropic, and no Anthropic staff moving to AISI, found in 14 searches. Jade Leung: search snippets (not read) show a GOV.UK headline 'Dr Jade Leung appointed vice chair of the AI Security Institute'; no Anthropic role found.
